name: Question 11
problem:
Let $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}]^{T}$ be a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the distribution of $Y=-{X}_{1}+{X}_{2}-2{X}_{3}.$
worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{k}]^{T}$ is a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y={c}^{T}X={\sum }_{i=1}^{k}{c}_{i}{X}_{i}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable, where $c$ is any $k\times 1$ column vector, and  

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu , \\ Var[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, since we wish to know the distribution of $Y=-{X}_{1}+{X}_{2}-2{X}_{3},$ we have 

$$
c=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, for the mean of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu  \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =-1+3+2 \\  & =4,\end{aligned}
$$

and for the variance of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -1 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =6-1+14 \\  & =19.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
Y∼N(4,19).
$$

Question 11
?

Let X=[X1,X2,X3]T be a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector μ and covariance matrix Σ given by μ=[13−1],Σ=[532341213]. Find the distribution of Y=−X1+X2−2X3.

a
N(4,7)
b
N(6,7)
c
N(4,19)
d
N(6,19)
e
N(2,21)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if X=[X1,X2,…,Xk]T is a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector μ and covariance matrix Σ, then the random variable Y, defined as

Y=cTX=∑i=1kciXi

is a normally distributed random variable, where c is any k×1 column vector, and

E[Y]=cTμ,Var[Y]=cTΣc.

In our case, since we wish to know the distribution of Y=−X1+X2−2X3, we have

c=[−11−2].

Therefore, for the mean of Y, we have

E[Y]=cTμ=[−11−2][13−1]=−1+3+2=4,

and for the variance of Y, we have

Var[Y]=cTΣc=[−11−2][532341213][−11−2]=[−11−2][−6−1−7]=6−1+14=19.

Therefore, we conclude that

Y∼N(4,19).
